songs.name: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Good Lovin’, Hard to Handle & tight Truckin’ medley
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a scorching Hard to Handle, a powerful Good Lovin' that bookends the first set, and an exhilarating Truckin > Not Fade Away > Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad > Not Fade Away sequence in the second set. Pigpen’s organ fuels many of the high points while the rhythm section keeps a solid groove. Recording quality ranges from good soundboard clarity to excellent stereo imaging, making the performance easy to enjoy.
ai_show_review.review:
February 24, 1971 at the Capitol Theater finds the Dead riding a wave of raw excitement that builds into one of their most memorable early‑70s outings. The first set kicks off with a tight Me And My Uncle and a fiery Cumberland Blues before diving into a blistering Hard To Handle where Pigpen’s gritty organ and harmonica push the band forward. Good Lovin' bookends the set, sandwiching a crisp drum break that leads straight into an inspired reprise; the guitar work here is surprisingly clear, especially on the Miller capture.

The second set keeps the momentum rolling with Sugar Magnolia and a spirited King Bee before launching into a marathon Truckin > Not Fade Away > Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad > Not Fade Away medley that feels both tight and adventurous. Pigpen’s loose‑but‑energetic organ shines on Turn On Your Lovelight, while Bill Kreutzmann holds down the groove in Mickey’s noticeable absence. Overall, the show balances high‑octane rockers with the kind of exploratory jams that make this era so compelling, and the best soundboard sources capture every nuance without sacrificing the band’s live feel.

best_recording.reason: Crisp soundboard capture that preserves the high‑energy performance and includes the full set, highlighting Hard To Handle and the expansive Truckin medley

key_highlights: Scorching Hard To Handle with Pigpen’s driving organ
Powerful Good Lovin' bookends the first set and showcases clear guitar tones
Exhilarating Truckin > Not Fade Away > Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad > Not Fade Away sequence
Excellent soundboard clarity on the Miller recording, especially for closing numbers
song_highlights: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

band_performance.Jerry: Early parts sound a bit choppy, but Garcia pushes hard later, delivering wah‑infused leads on the NFA/GDTR outro and crisp solos on Good Lovin'.
band_performance.Phil: Bass is often buried in the mix; however he surfaces briefly during Hard To Handle, providing a solid low‑end anchor when it matters.
band_performance.Bob: Weir slashes behind Garcia on Hard To Handle and stays tightly locked in throughout, with his rhythm work clearly defined in the Miller recording’s right channel.
band_performance.Brent: Pigpen’s organ and harmonica drive many of the night’s highlights, especially on Hard To Handle, Good Lovin', and Turn On Your Lovelight, adding a gritty, soulful texture.
band_performance.Mickey: His absence is felt early, contributing to a listless vibe in parts of the first set.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann keeps a steady foundation, stepping up as the show gains momentum and holding down the groove during the Truckin' medley.
